sentences.text: Ophthalmothule was a medium-sized plesiosaur measuring between 5 and 5.5 meters long, distinguished by its unusually large eye sockets.
Along with Abyssosaurus, this animal is one of the youngest known cryptoclidids from boreal regions.
The name Ophthalmothule means "eye of the north".
Researchers suggest the large eye sockets indicate a specialization for deep water and/or nocturnal hunting.
Ophthalmothule fossils were found in the Slottsmøya Member Lagerstätte of the Agardhfjellet Formation in Spitsbergen.
The genus Ophthalmothule was described by Roberts et al. in 2020, with the type species being Ophthalmothule cryostea.
Ophthalmothule is classified as a cryptoclidid plesiosaur, belonging to the family Cryptoclididae.
This animal belongs to the class Reptilia.
Ophthalmothule lived during the latest Volgian, around the Jurassic-Cretaceous boundary, with a time range from the Tithonian to the Berriasian, between 149.2 and 137.05 million years ago.
